title: Second Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for the Financial Year 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021
what_it_is: Second Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for the Financial Year 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021

sections.label: Migrant spouses income loss
sections.summary: An AWARE survey of 36 migrant spouses found 99% lost jobs or income since COVID-19 began.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head M of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to an AWARE survey with migrant spouses of Singaporean citizens in May, 99% of 36 respondents have either lost their jobs or seen a drastic decrease in income since the onset of COVID-19.

sections.label: Migrant spouses basic needs
sections.summary: Income loss makes meeting basic needs hard; a $300 Solidarity payment requires LTVP+ status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This widespread loss in income is making it difficult for many migrant spouses and their families to meet basic needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They can receive a $300 one-off Solidarity payment but only if they are on LTVP+.

sections.label: Transnational families Solidarity Payments
sections.summary: Transnational families receive $600 for the citizen member and $300 for the PR or LTVP+ spouse.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Transnational families would already be receiving support through the $600 Solidarity Payment to the citizen member, and $300 Solidarity Payment to the PR or LTVP+ spouse.

sections.label: COVID-19 mental distress surveys
sections.summary: WHO confirmed widespread psychological distress; surveys in China, the US and Singapore and SOS calls rose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed “widespread psychological distress” in COVID-19 affected populations, with mental distress being reported in 35% of the population surveyed in China and 45% in the United States.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: In an Ipsos survey of 1,000 Singaporeans between late April and early May, one in four respondents said they were not in good mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Our national suicide prevention hotline, operated by the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS), received 23% more calls in April from March.

sections.label: Singapore GDP forecast downgrade
sections.summary: Singapore's GDP growth forecasts were downgraded from -4% to -7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Singapore’s economic woes are likely to continue for the long term, as GDP growth forecasts have been downgraded from -4% to -7%.

sections.label: National CARE Hotline operations
sections.summary: The 24-hour National CARE Hotline began in April 2020, manned by volunteer professionals for mental health concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: A specific initiative developed is the new 24-hour National CARE Hotline (NCH).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The NCH, which came into operation in April 2020, is manned by volunteers comprising trained psychologists, counsellors, social workers and other professionals, and provides support to the larger community on mental health concerns, such as anxiety and adjustment issues related to COVID-19.

sections.label: Silver Generation Office senior outreach
sections.summary: The Silver Generation Office reached out to about 47,000 vulnerable seniors to refer them to assistance, including befriending and mental health services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For the elderly, the Silver Generation Office reached out to some 47,000 vulnerable seniors to refer them to assistance as required, including befriending and mental health services.

sections.label: MOH increased COVID-19 budget
sections.summary: In the Fortitude Budget, MOH has an increased budget to implement many COVID-19 management measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In this Fortitude Budget, MOH has an increased budget to implement many of the COVID-19 management measures.

sections.label: Deputy Prime Minister start-up funding
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced $285 million will be set aside to support promising start-ups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister announced that $285 million will be set aside to support “promising start-ups”.

sections.label: Start-up financing in Fortitude Budget
sections.summary: $285 million was set aside in the Fortitude Budget to provide financing support for promising start-ups, which contribute to new technologies and rejuvenation of traditional industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: They contribute to the development of new technologies and the rejuvenation of traditional industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We have set aside $285 million in the Fortitude Budget to provide financing support for promising start-ups.

sections.label: Special Situation Fund for Startups
sections.summary: The Special Situation Fund for Startups is intended to fill this gap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Special Situation Fund for Startups is intended to fill this gap.

sections.label: Government co-investment via convertible bonds
sections.summary: Under this scheme, the Government will co-invest in selected start-ups with the private sector on a one-to-one basis via convertible bonds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under this scheme, the Government will co-invest in the selected start-ups, together with the private sector, on a one-to-one basis via convertible bonds.

sections.label: SIRS versus Support Grant comparison
sections.summary: The passage states SIRS maximum cash assistance is $9,000 versus the Support Grant's $2,400, and SIRS inclusion is automatic while the Support Grant requires application.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe the Government has sought to address the different needs of each group in designing these schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the maximum cash assistance quantum at $9,000 is higher for the SIRS than for the Support Grant at $2,400.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Inclusion in SIRS is also automatic for qualifying Singaporeans, whereas the Support Grant must be applied for.

sections.label: Pandemic mental well-being of employees
sections.summary: The passage states the Fortitude Budget does not reference pandemic impact on employees' mental well-being and cites survey findings on mental health and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Not referenced in the Fortitude Budget is the impact of the pandemic on the mental well-being of employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: I have mentioned earlier that in a survey of business leaders and HR professionals, nearly one in two Singaporeans has had their mental health adversely affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: A recent survey also found that employees without managers attuned to their well-being are 61% more likely to say they have been less productive.

sections.label: Complaints over JSS misuse
sections.summary: The passage states MOM received complaints about companies not using JSS monies for employees, and IRAS said abusers may face Penal Code charges, imprisonment and a fine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: MOM has received complaints about companies taking JSS monies and not using them to support their employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: IRAS announced on 3 June 2020 that employers who abuse the JSS may be charged under the Penal Code and face imprisonment and a fine.

sections.label: Whistle-blowing protection and JSS payouts
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will consider a whistle-blowing protection law like the UK's regime and a mechanism for unaffected or profiting companies to return JSS payouts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: To empower employees to make complaints against errant employers and protect the most vulnerable in our workforce, will the Government consider a strong whistle-blowing protection law similar to the protected disclosures regime in the UK's employment Rights Act 1996 that is adequately communicated to all workers so that they are aware of the channels and feel safe exercising their right to whistle-blow.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Further, instead of relying on goodwill, should there be a mechanism to make companies that are unaffected by or even profiting from the crisis return their JSS payouts?

sections.label: SIRS beneficiaries and income criterion
sections.summary: The passage states SIRS has benefited over 120,000 SEPs, more than double usual Workfare recipients, and notes the income criterion and taxpayer income figures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: SIRS has now benefited over 120,000 SEPs – more than double the usual number of Workfare recipients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the income criterion serves as a proxy for their ability to save and, therefore, the likelihood of their ability to tide through periods of less earnings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: It should also be noted that about 80% of the personal income taxpayers earn incomes below the SIRS criterion of $100,000 a year or about $9,000 a month.

sections.label: AV criterion coverage of properties
sections.summary: The passage states the AV criterion of $21,000 covers about nine in 10 owner-occupied residential public and private properties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The AV criterion of $21,000 covers about nine in 10 owner-occupied residential public and private properties.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme and employer practices
sections.summary: Heng said the JSS amounted to $23.5 billion, protecting 1.9 million jobs, and the Government takes a serious view of unfair or fraudulent employment practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng recapped and shared with us that the JSS amounted to $23.5 billion, protecting 1.9 million jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Employers should act responsibly and fairly, and make sure that they are ensuring that their local workers are given wages even if they are unable to work.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I want to assure Ms Anthea Ong that the Government takes a very serious view of irresponsible, unfair or fraudulent employment practices, including false reporting of workers' CPF payments by employers to obtain higher JSS payouts.

sections.label: Penalties for errant employers
sections.summary: Employers who wrongfully dismiss workers may be ordered to pay compensation or reinstate them, and may lose employment support or Work Pass privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Employers who wrongfully dismiss their workers may be ordered to pay compensation or to reinstate workers to their former jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Errant employers may also see a withdrawal of Government-paid employment support or suspension of their Work Pass privileges.

sections.label: Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being
sections.summary: MOM announced a Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being, to be finalised in the second half of this year, with possible Employee Assistance Programme and insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply (COS) in March, Ms Ong will remember that MOM announced that we will formulate a Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being to educate our employers on basic mental health knowledge and make available the resources to help them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will work with the tripartite partners to evaluate the possibility of including an Employee Assistance Programme as well as insurance coverage for mental health as part of the upcoming Tripartite Advisory, which will be finalised in the second half of this year.

sections.label: JSS balance and SME benefits
sections.summary: The JSS strikes a balance between targeted assistance and administrative efficiency, with two-thirds of SMEs benefiting from the $23.5 billion scheme protecting 1.9 million jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: So, we strike a good balance between targeted assistance and administrative efficiency in designing the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And earlier on, when he reminded us that the JSS amounted to $23.5 billion protecting 1.9 million jobs, two-thirds of our SMEs benefit from this.

sections.label: Severe action on fraudulent employment practices
sections.summary: The Government will deal severely with irresponsible, unfair or fraudulent employment practices, including false reporting of CPF contributions, and will not hesitate to act.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Low, can you just wrap up quickly?

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure Ms Ong that any irresponsible or unfair, fraudulent employment practises, including a false reporting of CPF contributions and so on will be dealt with severely and we will not hesitate to take actions accordingly.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant funding
sections.summary: The Government signalled the COVID-19 Support Grant is an important piece of COVID-19 welfare schemes by pumping in $800 million as part of the Fortitude Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has signalled that the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) is an important piece in the array of COVID-19 welfare schemes by pumping in $800 million as part of the Fortitude Budget.

sections.label: CSG eligibility gaps and recommendations
sections.summary: The speaker says people without bank accounts or daily-rated workers are excluded from CSG and recommends lowering the income-loss period to one month and widening eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Crucially, members of society in precarious positions are excluded from CSG, such as individuals with no bank account or daily-rated workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I recommend that the Government reduce the required period for involuntary no pay leave or duration of income loss from three consecutive months to one month and allow individuals with no bank account and daily-rated or ad hoc workers to be eligible for CSG.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant criteria
sections.summary: CSG supports lower to middle income Singaporeans or Permanent Residents who are involuntarily unemployed, on involuntary no-pay leave for three months, or with reduced salary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) supports lower to middle income Singaporeans or Permanent Residents who, as a result of the economic impact of COVID-19, are presently (a) involuntarily unemployed due to retrenchment or contract termination; (b) placed on involuntary no-pay leave (NPL) for at least three consecutive months; or (c) experiencing reduced monthly salary of at least 30% for at least three consecutive months.

sections.label: ComCare assistance and income criteria
sections.summary: New ComCare recipients generally get at least six months of assistance, and SMTA and Interim Assistance require monthly household income of $1,900 or less or per capita income of $650 or less.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In general, those who are newly placed on ComCare will receive at least six months of assistance, which provides them with a longer runway to regain stability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) and Interim Assistance have income eligibility criteria of a monthly household income of $1,900 and below or per capita household income of $650 and below.

sections.label: CSG application period and review
sections.summary: CSG applications run from May 2020 to September 2020, and the Government will keep reviewing support schemes as the COVID-19 situation evolves.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: While CSG is open for applications from May 2020 till September 2020, the Government will continue to review our support schemes for those who need help, taking into account how the COVID-19 situation evolves.
